about: I Am the Danger / I Am the One Who Knocks stacks three close-ups of Walter White (Bryan Cranston) from Breaking Bad, staring down at his wife Skyler with a clenched, contemptuous face, each panel captioned like a TV subtitle. The meme copies the rhythm of his monologue: a calm correction in the first panel, a scornful rhetorical question in the middle, and a cold one-line declaration at the end. People swap the lines to make any small or ordinary thing sound like the most menacing force in the room, from a cat who knocks cups off tables to the intern who has production access.
origin: The speech comes from the Breaking Bad season 4 episode "Cry Me a Maudlin" (2011), where Skyler begs Walt to go to the police because she thinks he is in danger. He answers that he is not in danger, he is the danger, and finishes with "I am the one who knocks." Clips and subtitled stills of the scene became a lasting reaction format, and Samuel L. Jackson even performed the monologue for a 2013 charity video.
usage:
There are three yellow subtitle boxes, one under each panel. The first box flips the worry: "I am not in danger, X. I am the danger." The middle box is the long, scornful line that dismisses whatever the other person imagined. The last box is the short, chilling punchline in the "I am the one who..." pattern.

It is funniest when the speaker is something small, harmless or mundane talking with full Heisenberg menace: a pet, a bug in the code, a group chat admin, a smoke detector at 3am. Keep the third line the shortest so it lands like a mic drop, and write the captions in sentence case so they read like real subtitles.

For just the final line on one frame, use the single-panel I Am the One Who Knocks template.
ideas: I am not in danger, Skyler. I am the danger.
A guy opens his door and gets shot, and you think that of me? No.
I am the one who knocks.
I am not in danger of failing, professor. I am the failure.
A student skips one lecture and you think that's me? No.
I am the one who skips all of them.
I am not breaking production. I am the production bug.
A test fails and you think it's flaky? No.
I am the one who deploys on Friday.
I am not in the way. I am the way.
A glass falls off the table and you think it was an accident? No.
I am the one who pushes.
I am not low on battery. I am the battery.
A phone dies at 12 percent and you blame the cold? No.
I am the one who drains.
I am not in the group chat. I am the group chat.
A message gets left on read and you think it's busy? No.
I am the one who leaves you on read.
